doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Club hours and the pimps who set up the bar
summary: Gigs ran 10 to 4 or 5 a.m.; late-night spenders like Joe Louis extended the sets.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What was the schedule like at the clubs? 10 to 5?
10 to 4 a.m. in New York and about 10 to 5 in Brooklyn.
How many sets would that be?

Well, what would happen was this. We’d hit at 10. We’d play 2 or 3 sets, and then we’d try to stretch it. But eventually, what would happen, about 3 or 4 o’clock, the pimps would come in with their women. They’d got the money. They’d come in and set up the bar, and the man said, “Well, they set up the bar; you’ve got to play a little extra.” So we ended up playing til 5 o’clock.
Joe Louis would come in there, and then everybody’d see him and then run to Joe, and Joe, you know how he was: “Give everybody a drink!” So the man said, “You’ve got to play a little set for Joe.”
So you were playing for a full spectrum of society.
